newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM Q1 operating profits more than triple.
newsitem.headline: KLM Q1 operating profits more than triple.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said on Tuesday sharply higher traffic and improved cost controls had helped to more than triple operating income in its first 1997/98 quarter ended June 30.
First-quarter operating profit soared to 244 million guilders from a year-earlier 80 million, while net profits fell to 190 million from a year-earlier 271 million.

Last year's net profits were inflated by a 245 million guilder contribution from the revaluation of preference shares in U.S. partner Northwest Airlines, while this year's bottom line was eroded by a hefty 74 million guilder tax bill.
The shares rose on the results, putting on 1.40 guilders to 77.80 by 1030 GMT, in a slightly higher Amsterdam bourse.
KLM said it expected operating profits for the full 1997/98 financial year, ending March 30, to improve on previous years.
"As far as operating income for the full fiscal year is concerned, we expect to appromimate the level attained in the better years in KLM's recent history," it said.
Analysts had expected the airline to post a first quarter net profit of between 94 and 136 million guilders.
